inputs.name: SecureChannelService.constructor.options
inputs.description: Configuration binding a host or device role to the host and device IDs, local static key pair, and pinned peer key. Host generation defaults to 0; chunkBytes and messageBytes default to remoteLimits.chunkBytes (131072) and remoteLimits.messageBytes (16777216), while absent ephemeral and nonce values are generated by remoteKeys() and randomBytes(16); examples are omitted because the value contains CryptoKey and Uint8Array instances.

inputs.name: SecureChannelService.answer.hello
inputs.description: The peer hello packet supplied to the host. answer requires type hello and a deviceId equal to options.deviceId, then uses the packet nonce and ephemeral key to derive session keys.

inputs.name: SecureChannelService.accept.packet
inputs.description: The host accept packet supplied to the device after its hello has started. accept requires device role, a local nonce, and no existing session keys, then derives keys from this packet nonce, ephemeral key, and generation.

inputs.name: SecureChannelService.seal.text
inputs.description: Plain message to seal and emit as consecutive sealed packets. Its encoded byte length cannot exceed limits.messageBytes or the default remoteLimits.messageBytes (16777216).

inputs.name: SecureChannelService.seal.emit
inputs.description: Callback invoked once for each generated sealed packet, in the order the packets must be sent. Each packet carries its counter, continuation flag, and base64url ciphertext plus authentication tag; chunks use limits.chunkBytes or the default remoteLimits.chunkBytes (131072).

inputs.name: SecureChannelService.open.packet
inputs.description: Next packet received from the peer. It must be sealed with exactly the next receive counter; partial messages return null while more is true, and the assembled message is limited by messageBytes.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.ready
outputs.description: Whether session keys have been derived. It is false before answer or accept completes and becomes false again when an opening violation clears the keys.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.hello
outputs.description: The device first-packet hello, containing version 1, the configured device ID, a base64url P-256 ephemeral public key, and a 16-byte nonce. It is available only to a device and only once per instance; it does not mean the session keys are ready.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.answer
outputs.description: The host accept packet, containing its ephemeral public key and nonce and the generation bound into the derived session keys. It is available only to a host and only once per instance; generation defaults to 0.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.accept
outputs.description: Completes device-side session-key derivation from the host accept packet and resolves without a value. It requires a prior device hello and no existing session keys.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.seal
outputs.description: Completes after sealing the message and passing its packets to emit in send order. Message size is bounded by options.limits?.messageBytes ?? remoteLimits.messageBytes, and chunks by options.limits?.chunkBytes ?? remoteLimits.chunkBytes.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.open
outputs.description: Yields null for a packet marked more, then yields the decoded message text when its final packet is authenticated and assembled. Packets must use the strict next counter, and the full message cannot exceed the configured or default message-byte limit.

errors.name: SecureFailure
errors.description: Thrown for handshake role or state violations, malformed or mismatched packets, out-of-order counters, authentication failures, and message-size or decoded-text violations. Its reason is state, packet, counter, tag, or size; failures detected while opening a packet clear the session keys.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: An expected CLI error propagated while a channel operation is running. Errors caught during key derivation or authenticated packet opening are converted to SecureFailure.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.ready
outputs.description: Whether session keys have been derived. It is false before answer or accept completes and becomes false again when an opening violation clears the keys.

outputs.name: SecureChannelService.hello

errors.name: SecureFailure
errors.description: Thrown with reason state when the configured role is not device or hello has already started the handshake.

errors.description: Thrown with reason state before session keys are ready, packet for a non-sealed or undecodable message, counter for an out-of-order packet, tag for failed authentication, or size when the assembled message exceeds its byte limit; these opening violations clear session keys.

outputs.description: The constructed SecureChannelService instance, retaining the supplied options and initializing handshake, counters, message assembly, and operation queues. A class instance cannot be represented as a JSON example.
